text:
incident-bot: HIGH -> GPU THERMAL + ECC spike on cluster-gpu-us-east-1 (nodes: gpu-nd-17, gpu-nd-18). Paging eng-oncall. metric: gpu_temperature_celsius > 87C, ecc_corrected_count increased by 120/min on 2 nodes :fire:

alex: ack — I'm on pager for this one, grabbing logs and node status now.

maria: I can take once you confirm it's not a noisy metric. last week we saw duplicate sensors on gpu-nd-17. @alex can you confirm host-agent version?

alex: host-agent v2.3.1 on both nodes. running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits` shows temps 89/91C, util 92%/88%, vram used 98%/96%. VRAM pressure looks real.

jay: 2 quick asks: are these serving nodes (prod) or batch? and any customer-facing errors?

alex: prod-serving for big-embeddings route. SLO doc says degrade tolerant but we hit tail latencies for some customers. No 5xx yet, but observed token generation rate dropouts and worker restarts.

maria: ok — sounds like thermal-induced throttling + possible ECC leading to kernel resets. Steps: 1) cordon/evacuate one node at a time 2) lower batch size / route to fallback model 3) mute noisy alert temporarily while we tune.

kat: +1. I'll start a live mitigation plan in the incident thread (short checklist). Also adding customer-impact note to the incident ticket: some customers on embeddings may see 200-800ms extra tail latency.

alex: cordoning gpu-nd-17 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-nd-17 && kubectl drain gpu-nd-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — evictions in progress.

sre-bot: automation: started drain on gpu-nd-17 (pods evicted: 6). Estimated finish 90s.

jay: while drain runs, can we reduce concurrency on embeddings route? Suggest config change: `max_concurrent_requests: 6 -> 3` for embeddings-prod-blue. That will reduce per-GPU memory pressure.

maria: deployed runtime patch to lower batch_size and concurrency on embeddings-prod-blue. Confirming rollout now.

alex: drain finished for gpu-nd-17. Node temp dropped to idle 45C after reboot of some drivers. ECC corrected count: reset after reboot.

kat: good. gpu-nd-18 still hot — planning to move remaining load to dedicated warm pool and schedule maintenance for both nodes (sensor swap + firmware).

jay: post-incident tuning items we should capture here:
- reduce alert sensitivity: change thermal alert from 5m avg > 87C to 10m avg > 90C for pages (short spikes shouldn't page).
- convert `ecc_corrected_count > 50/min` to warning -> page only if `ecc_uncorrectable > 0` or `ecc_corrected_count` sustained for 15m.
- add VRAM saturation rule: `gpu_vram_used_ratio > 0.95 for 5m` => page (currently only warns).
- add node-drain-rate anomaly: detect >3 node drains in 30m and escalate.

maria: agree. also add dashboard panels: per-node time-series for temperature, ECC corrected/uncorrected, vram ratio, and per-container memory usage to help root-cause.

alex: I can submit PR to alerts repo with the prometheus rule diffs. proposed alert snippet (draft):
```yaml
- alert: GPUHighTemperaturePage
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_temperature_celsius[10m]) > 90
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU temp sustained >90C on {{ $labels.instance }}"

- alert: GPUVramSaturation
  expr: max_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes[5m]) > 0.95
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

kat: also add runbook link and an aggregated incident tag `gpu-thermal-ecc` so ops playbooks can be searched.

sre-bot: noted. creating ticket REDWOOD-INC-4523: "gpu thermal/ecc spike — tuning + dash" and adding assignees alex, maria, jay.

maria: one more operational change: reduce page noise by routing thermal warnings to #eng-sre-warnings and pages only on combined condition: `thermal > threshold AND (vram>0.94 OR ecc_uncorrectable>0)` — avoids pages on transient high util.

jay: +1 on combined condition. For short-term, can we mute `gpu_temperature_high` paging rule for 2 hours while nodes finish maintenance? We should document the mute window and owner.

alex: muting `gpu_temperature_high` pages for 2h and created calendar entry: `GPU-Maintenance-Win (2h)` with owner @alex.

kat: followups (post-incident):
- hardware ticket to infra: sensor replacement + driver firmware check
- alert PR to alerts repo: (jay/alex)
- dashboard PR to grafana: (maria)
- runbook update: add explicit steps for draining and warm-pool routing (kat)
- customer comms draft if degradation persists >4h (ops/growth)

alex: leaving detailed logs in ticket. thanks all. I'll hand off to @maria for next shift monitoring.

maria: taking handoff. I'll monitor metrics and confirm post-maintenance stability. If we see ECC uncorrectable errors, I'll escalate to infra-hardware and page immediately. :thumbsup:
